gaps.sentence: We had ___ awful weather on the crossing.
gaps.explanation: 'Weather' is uncountable — 'had awful weather', no article.

gaps.sentence: He gave me ___ useful advice about the paperwork.
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable — never 'an advice'. Use 'a piece of advice' for one item.

gaps.sentence: ___ honesty is the best policy, as the saying goes.
gaps.explanation: Abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article: honesty, happiness, love.

gaps.sentence: He was ___ last person to leave the building.
gaps.explanation: Ordinals take 'the': the last person, the first time.

gaps.sentence: They're building ___ new library near the town hall.
gaps.explanation: A new library — first mention; the town hall is the known one.

gaps.sentence: She works as ___ editor for a travel magazine.
She earns fifty pounds ___ hour as a consultant.
gaps.explanation: 'An hour' — the 'h' is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: ___ books you left on my desk were really useful.
gaps.explanation: 'The books you left…' — the clause identifies which books.
